# pve_guest_firewall_rules (Resource)

Manages the ordered firewall ruleset of one guest (`GET/POST /nodes/{node}/{qemu,lxc}/{vmid}/firewall/rules`, `GET/PUT/DELETE .../rules/{pos}`). The `rules` list in configuration is authoritative: applies converge PVE to exactly this list and order, removing or rewriting entries made out of band. PVE renumbers positions, so `pos` is computed and resynced after every apply.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "pve_guest_firewall_rules" "vm100" {
  node       = "pve1"
  guest_type = "qemu"
  vmid       = 100
  rules = [
    {
      type    = "in"
      action  = "ACCEPT"
      proto   = "tcp"
      dport   = "443"
      iface   = "net0"
      comment = "HTTPS"
    },
    {
      type    = "out"
      action  = "ACCEPT"
      comment = "Allow all outbound"
    },
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `guest_type` (String) Guest type: `qemu` for virtual machines, `lxc` for containers. Must be one of: `qemu`, `lxc`. Changing this value forces recreation.
- `node` (String) The cluster node hosting the guest. Changing this value forces recreation.
- `rules` (Attributes List) The ordered firewall rules. Order is significant: PVE evaluates rules top to bottom and the first match wins. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rules))
- `vmid` (Number) The guest ID. Must be between 100 and 999999999 inclusive. Changing this value forces recreation.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Identifier of the ruleset; `<node>:<guest_type>:<vmid>`.

<a id="nestedatt--rules"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rules`

Required:

- `action` (String) Rule action (`ACCEPT`, `DROP`, `REJECT`) or, for `type = "group"`, the name of the referenced security group. PVE validates the value as an identifier: 2-20 characters, starting with a letter, then letters, digits, `-` or `_`.
- `type` (String) Rule direction. `group` entries reference a security group via `action`. Must be one of: `in`, `out`, `forward`, `group`.

Optional:

- `comment` (String) Descriptive comment.
- `dest` (String) Restrict packet destination address: a single IP address or CIDR network, an IP set (`+ipsetname`), an alias name, an address range like `10.0.0.1-10.0.0.10`, or a comma-separated list. Do not mix IPv4 and IPv6 entries in one list.
- `dport` (String) Restrict TCP/UDP destination port: a service name or number (0-65535), a range like `80:85`, or a comma-separated list of ports and ranges. Only meaningful together with a TCP/UDP `proto` or macro.
- `enable` (Boolean) Whether the rule is active. PVE stores this flag as 0/1.
- `icmp_type` (String) Restrict the ICMP type (e.g. `echo-request`). Only valid when `proto` is `icmp` or `icmpv6`/`ipv6-icmp`.
- `iface` (String) Network interface name. On guest rulesets use the guest configuration key names (`net0`, `net1`, ...); node and cluster rulesets accept arbitrary host interface names.
- `log` (String) Log level for the rule. Must be one of: `emerg`, `alert`, `crit`, `err`, `warning`, `notice`, `info`, `debug`, `nolog`.
- `macro` (String) Use a predefined standard macro (e.g. `SSH`, `HTTP`, `SMB`, `Ping`); PVE expands it into implicit port/protocol matches. PVE accepts the names returned by `GET /cluster/firewall/macros`, so the provider passes the value through without validation.
- `proto` (String) IP protocol: a protocol name (`tcp`, `udp`, `icmp`, `icmpv6`/`ipv6-icmp`, ...) or a number as defined in `/etc/protocols`. PVE accepts names and numbers without a fixed whitelist, so the provider passes the value through.
- `source` (String) Restrict packet source address: a single IP address or CIDR network, an IP set (`+ipsetname`), an alias name, an address range like `10.0.0.1-10.0.0.10`, or a comma-separated list. Do not mix IPv4 and IPv6 entries in one list.
- `sport` (String) Restrict TCP/UDP source port: a service name or number (0-65535), a range like `80:85`, or a comma-separated list of ports and ranges. Only meaningful together with a TCP/UDP `proto` or macro.

Read-Only:

- `ipversion` (Number) IP version (4 or 6), determined by PVE from `source`/`dest`; null when the rule does not restrict addresses.
- `pos` (Number) Rule position in the ruleset (0-based). PVE assigns and renumbers positions, so the provider resyncs it from the ruleset after every apply; the list order in configuration is authoritative.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import an existing guest firewall ruleset by `<node>:<guest_type>:<vmid>`:
terraform import pve_guest_firewall_rules.vm100 pve1:qemu:100
```
